---
title: "EU FDI Screening From 17 January 2028: What the Notification Numbers Say About In-Depth Review Risk"
description: "Using European Commission figures to quantify the chance that a notified foreign direct investment enters an in-depth security risk assessment before the 17 January 2028 rules apply."
date: 2026-10-19
tags:
  - EU FDI screening
  - regulatory compliance
  - imports
  - supply chain
source: "European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security"
---

The EU foreign direct investment screening rules will apply from **17 January 2028**. For an importer, investor, or business planning a transaction that touches the EU market, the practical question is not only whether a notification is required. It is how likely a filing is to leave the fast track and become an in-depth security risk assessment.

The European Commission's Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security reports figures that make that risk measurable.

## The notification baseline

The Commission received **667 foreign direct investment notifications** under the EU cooperation mechanism. That volume followed a **40% increase in notifications** to the mechanism. The prior comparison point in the same figures is **477 notifications**.

The arithmetic is straightforward:

- 477 earlier notifications
- 667 notifications in the reported period
- an increase of 190 notifications
- a reported 40% increase in notification volume

That matters because the 17 January 2028 application date arrives after a period in which the cooperation mechanism is already handling substantially more cases. A business should not plan around the assumption that notification is a rare, low-volume process.

## Most cases close within 15 calendar days

The Commission reports that **88% of notified cases were closed within 15 calendar days**. On 667 notifications, that is the large majority: roughly 587 cases.

The remaining 12% is the group that matters for transaction planning. The Commission says **12% of notified investments required an in-depth security risk assessment**. Applied to 667 notifications, that is about 80 investments.

That gives a simple planning ratio:

| Outcome | Reported share | Approximate number among 667 notifications |
|---|---:|---:|
| Closed within 15 calendar days | 88% | About 587 |
| In-depth security risk assessment | 12% | About 80 |

The percentages are reported Commission figures. The counts are arithmetic from those percentages and the reported total, so they should be read as approximate case counts rather than separately published exact totals.

## Manufacturing is the largest exposed sector in the in-depth group

Not every in-depth case is equally distributed across industries. The Commission reports that **manufacturing accounted for 53% of in-depth assessment cases**.

Using the approximate 80-investment in-depth group, 53% corresponds to roughly 42 manufacturing cases. In other words, manufacturing is not merely present in the in-depth caseload; it represents more than half of it.

For an importer or investor with manufacturing assets, EU production facilities, critical inputs, or technology-linked operations, the relevant sequence is:

1. notification enters the EU cooperation mechanism;
2. most cases close within 15 calendar days;
3. about 12 in every 100 notified investments move to an in-depth security risk assessment;
4. within that higher-risk group, manufacturing cases make up 53%.

This is not a statement that every manufacturing transaction is reviewed in depth. It is a statement about concentration: when the Commission does open a deeper assessment, manufacturing cases are the largest part of that group.

## Opinions remain rare, but they are not the only compliance cost

The Commission issued opinions in **less than 2% of cases**. On a base of 667 notifications, less than 2% means fewer than roughly 14 cases.

That number should not be confused with the 12% in-depth assessment rate. An in-depth security risk assessment is substantially more common than a Commission opinion. A transaction can therefore face delay, information requests, and scrutiny even when the process does not end in the Commission issuing an opinion.

The published figures do not include a filing fee, legal-fee schedule, delay cost, or transaction-value threshold. As a result, this article cannot calculate a euro amount per shipment, per filing, or per day of review. Adding such a number would require a source that sets the relevant rate or amount.

What the figures do support is a probability-based timeline:

- **88%** of notified cases closed within **15 calendar days**;
- **12%** required an in-depth security risk assessment;
- **53%** of those in-depth cases were manufacturing cases;
- Commission opinions occurred in **less than 2%** of all cases.

## What to calculate before 17 January 2028

A business should treat the 15-calendar-day outcome as the majority case, not the guaranteed case. With a 12% in-depth rate, a planner cannot fund or schedule a transaction as if every notification will close within 15 calendar days.

The useful internal calculation is:

`notification volume × 12% = expected number of in-depth assessments`

For a portfolio with 10 notified investments, 12% means planning capacity for roughly one in-depth case, even though the actual outcome is binary for each filing. For manufacturing-heavy portfolios, the concentration is more severe because manufacturing represents 53% of the in-depth group.

The 17 January 2028 date therefore has a concrete operational meaning. Companies should identify reportable transactions early, prepare the information needed for notification, and reserve additional time for the roughly one-in-eight chance of an in-depth assessment. The cost figure missing from the official material is currency; the risk figure is not.

The EU FDI screening rules apply from **17 January 2028**. That date gives businesses a fixed compliance deadline, but the caseload is already growing.

Before the rules apply on **17 January 2028**, the numbers point to a clear planning rule: expect most EU FDI notifications to close within **15 calendar days**, but reserve time and resources for the **12%** that enter in-depth review.
